authoredFrom: ER2 reference surface (user findings #2/#4/#6, closes ER-G1/G2/G5; rulings ER-D8/D9/D11/D14) authored from the pinned grammar probe (2026-09-18) before this fixture's F3 run: ?MACRO uses emit references -> the macro name per-site (a use of a header-defined macro is still a use - ?SERVER_HEADER lands as an external, honest); fun values are references, never calls (the call happens at apply time); -callback emits a Method symbol owned by the module with the sig's arity; ?MODULE in remote-module position expands to the current module (the one predefined macro whose meaning is unambiguous) while the ?MODULE use itself still emits its macro reference; type syntax (the callback's state()) is DECL-ONLY - never a calls edge. ER3 (2026-09-25, from the M12 differential, which caught two fabricated dependencies): -type/-opaque emit references only where a type APPLIES a name - a call head (binary(), atom(), term()) or a record type's own name (#ctx{} -> ctx) - so a bare unquoted atom in type syntax is the atom LITERAL of that name (monday | tuesday declares no dependency; writing `integer` without parens is the atom integer, not the type integer()) and a map/record field key is a DECLARATION (the keys of #{id := binary()} are not references - the ER2 authoring counted every bare atom and produced job -> id / job -> kind). A remote type keeps its qualification (dict:dict() -> dict:dict, ER-D1), a record TYPE is a declaration and never an instantiates (the same DECL-ONLY boundary as calls), and the field types inside a record type are walked (ctx_rec -> pid).
